title: Merge Videos Online – Join Clips Free, No Upload
description: Join two or more video clips into one MP4 or WebM in your browser. Put them in order, pick the size, keep the sound. Nothing is uploaded.
heading: Merge Videos into One
subtitle: Put your clips in order and join them into one MP4 or WebM video, right in your browser.
intro: Join phone clips, screen recordings or parts of a longer film into one video. Drag the clips into the order you want, choose the picture size, and merge. Clips of a different shape get black bars instead of being stretched or cut, and the sound of every clip plays with its picture.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your clips are joined by your own browser and never sent to a server.

features.title: Any mix of clips
features.text: MP4, MOV, WebM and MKV clips of different sizes join into one video with black bars where the shapes differ.

features.title: Your order
features.text: Drag the clips or use the arrows to set the order before you merge.

steps.title: Add your clips
steps.text: Choose two or more videos; add more at any time.

steps.title: Set the order
steps.text: Drag the clips, or use the up and down arrows.

steps.title: Choose size and format
steps.text: Keep the first clip’s size or pick 1080p or 720p, and MP4 or WebM.

steps.title: Merge and download
steps.text: Click Merge videos, watch the result and download it.

handles: Input: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, M4V and other videos your browser can play.
Output: MP4 (H.264) or WebM (VP9 or VP8), whichever your browser can make.
Size: the first clip’s size, 1080p or 720p, following the first clip’s orientation.
Sound: kept by default; a clip without sound plays silence for its length.
limits: Every clip is encoded again, so merging takes about as long as the videos play on a slow device.
Very long or 4K videos are limited by your device’s memory.
There are no transitions between clips; one cuts straight to the next.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The joining is done by your own browser, on your device, with the video encoders built into it. Nothing is sent to a server; open your browser's network panel while it runs and you will see no upload.

faq.question: Can I merge videos of different sizes?
faq.answer: Yes. Every clip is fitted into the size you choose and keeps its shape; the space around a clip of another shape is filled with black bars.

faq.question: Can I merge a MOV from an iPhone with an MP4?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as your browser can play both. Chrome and Edge read the most formats; HEVC clips need a browser that plays HEVC.

faq.question: Can I merge videos without the sound?
faq.answer: Yes. Untick Keep sound and the result has no sound track.

faq.question: Which browsers does it work in?
faq.answer: Recent Chrome and Edge read and make the most formats; Safari and Firefox work with most videos. If your browser can't read or make a codec, the page names it and says what to try instead.

faq.question: Is it free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.
